summary.text: A female patient (age 62) with melanoma received nivolumab and ipilimumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis alongside systemic irAE of adrenal failure. Ocular symptoms began 13 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as partial response.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 1+, OS 2+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.8, OS 0.7 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3, with granulomatous inflammation and VKH disease–like uveitis. Vitiligo and poliosis were described as extraocular symptoms. The follow-up period was 16 months.

Ocular treatment was oral steroids and STTA. ICI therapy was discontinued temporarily because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.4, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale; ocular complication recorded: choroidal neovascularization. Intravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor injections were given for choroidal neovascularization, with limited visual improvement.

summary.text: A female patient (age 53) with breast cancer received pembrolizumab and developed ICI-associated anterior uveitis alongside systemic irAE of arthralgia. Ocular symptoms began 353 days after ICI administration, with unilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as not applicable.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OS 1+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OS 0.08 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3. The follow-up period was 6 months.
Ocular treatment was oral steroids. ICI therapy had already been completed as scheduled. Final best corrected visual acuity was OS 0.8 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A female patient (age 50) with uterine cancer received pembrolizumab and developed ICI-associated posterior uveitis alongside systemic irAE of thyroiditis and dermatitis. Ocular symptoms began 73 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as not evaluable.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 0, OS 0, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3 and VKH disease–like uveitis. The follow-up period was 8 months.
Ocular treatment was oral steroids. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of a systemic irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A female patient (age 84) with melanoma received pembrolizumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis. Ocular symptoms began 335 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as progressive disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 2+, OS 2+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.2, OS 0.5 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3 and VKH disease–like uveitis. The follow-up period was 6 months.

Ocular treatment was Sub-Tenon’s capsule triamcinolone acetonide injection (STTA). ICI therapy was discontinued temporarily because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.4, OS 0.6 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A male patient (age 51) with melanoma received pembrolizumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis. Ocular symptoms began 952 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as complete response.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 2+, OS 0.5+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 0.7 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3, with granulomatous inflammation. The follow-up period was 53 months.

Ocular treatment was Sub-Tenon’s capsule triamcinolone acetonide injection (STTA). ICI therapy was discontinued temporarily because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 1.0 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A female patient (age 54) with melanoma received nivolumab and developed ICI-associated anterior uveitis alongside systemic irAE of hepatopathy. Ocular symptoms began 59 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as progressive disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 0, OS 0.5+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.0, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 1, with granulomatous inflammation. The follow-up period was 2 months.
Ocular treatment was observation. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of a systemic irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 0.9 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A male patient (age 40) with Hodgkin’s lymphoma received nivolumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis alongside systemic irAE of dermatitis. Ocular symptoms began 228 days after ICI administration, with unilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as Unknown.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 0.5+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.4 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3. The follow-up period was 10 months.

Ocular treatment was oral steroids. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.05 on the decimal scale; ocular complication recorded: Hypotony maculopathy. Final visual acuity of 20/40 or worse was attributed to hypotony maculopathy.

summary.text: A male patient (age 67) with renal cancer received nivolumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis alongside systemic irAE of diarrhea. Ocular symptoms began 121 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as Unknown.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 0.5+, OS 1+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.3, OS 0.4 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3. The follow-up period was 19 months.
Ocular treatment was steroid eye drops. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.9, OS 0.7 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A male patient (age 65) with renal cancer received nivolumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis. Ocular symptoms began 67 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as partial response.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 1+, OS 0, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3, with granulomatous inflammation and VKH disease–like uveitis. The follow-up period was 2 months.
Ocular treatment was steroid eye drops. ICI therapy was discontinued temporarily because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A female patient (age 80) with gastric cancer received nivolumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis. Ocular symptoms began 332 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as stable disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 2+, OS 2+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.5, OS 0.5 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3, with granulomatous inflammation and VKH disease–like uveitis. The follow-up period was 23 months.
Ocular treatment was oral steroids and STTA. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.0, OS 1.2 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A male patient (age 70) with esophageal cancer received nivolumab and developed ICI-associated optic neuritis. Ocular symptoms began 40 days after ICI administration, with unilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as progressive disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 0, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.004 (described in the text as finger counting) on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 4. The follow-up period was 1 months.

Ocular treatment was steroid pulse therapy. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.5 on the decimal scale; ocular complication recorded: Optic atrophy. The optic neuritis developed after three cycles of nivolumab; initial visual acuity was described as finger counting, and after three courses of steroid pulse therapy it improved to 20/40. Visual acuity of 20/40 or worse at final observation was attributed to optic neuritis.

summary.text: A female patient (age 77) with melanoma received nivolumab and ipilimumab and developed ICI-associated sclerouveitis alongside systemic irAE of hepatopathy. Ocular symptoms began 12 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as progressive disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 1+, OS 1+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.5, OS 0.4 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 2, with granulomatous inflammation. The follow-up period was 10 months.
Ocular treatment was oral steroids. ICI therapy was discontinued temporarily because of a systemic irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.3, OS 0.3 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A male patient (age 31) with melanoma received nivolumab and ipilimumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis alongside systemic irAE of hypophysitis. Ocular symptoms began 61 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as Unknown.

summary.text: A female patient (age 63) with melanoma received nivolumab and ipilimumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis alongside systemic irAE of myocarditis, hepatopathy and dermatitis. Ocular symptoms began 24 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as stable disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 1+, OS 1+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 0.4 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 3, with granulomatous inflammation and VKH disease–like uveitis. The follow-up period was 16 months.
Ocular treatment was oral steroids. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of a systemic irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 1.2, OS 0.4 on the decimal scale.

summary.text: A female patient (age 72) with melanoma received nivolumab and ipilimumab and developed ICI-associated panuveitis alongside systemic irAE of hepatopathy and thyroiditis. Ocular symptoms began 12 days after ICI administration, with bilateral ocular involvement. Tumor response to ICI was recorded as stable disease.

At the initial visit anterior chamber cell grades were OD 1+, OS 1+, and initial best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.09, OS 0.2 on the decimal scale. The ocular irAE was CTCAE grade 4, with granulomatous inflammation. The follow-up period was 15 months.

Ocular treatment was oral steroids. ICI therapy was discontinued permanently because of an ocular irAE. Final best corrected visual acuity was OD 0.1, OS 0.4 on the decimal scale; ocular complication recorded as suspected optic neuropathy in the table and suspected optic neuritis in the text (source conflict). Systemic corticosteroid therapy was given but visual function remained poor, and final visual acuity was 20/40 or worse.

article_limitations: Retrospective single-center case series; patient numbers follow first mention in the source (patient 15 is named in the results text before Table 1), so patient ids p1..p16 do not match the table row numbers.
Blank or dash cells (systemic irAE, granulomatous inflammation, VKH disease-like uveitis, ocular complications) are not recorded as absence because the table has no legend stating their meaning.

HLA genotyping in two VKH disease-like uveitis patients, the one patient who improved spontaneously with ICI discontinuation alone, the six topical-only patients and the systemic steroid indications are described without naming patients and are not assigned to individuals.

Table 2 and the discussion are cohort-level statistics and literature comparisons and are not copied to individuals; Japanese ethnicity is recorded from the cohort sentence that explicitly covers all 16 patients.
Table 1 does not print a unit for individual ages (Age/sex column); only the cohort mean is stated in years, so individual ages carry no unit.
Case 16 ocular complication is a source conflict between suspected optic neuropathy (table) and suspected optic neuritis (text).
The article has no figures and no supplements.
